pearls: Any patient contact that does not result in transport requires documentation and disposition.
Minimum required vital signs on every patient include BP, Pulse, Respiratory rate, Pulse oximetry, and Pain severity.
Pulse oximetry, glucose measurement, and temperature documentation is dependent on complaint.
Timing of transport based on patient's clinical condition.

steps.text: Scene Safety & BSI (body substance isolation).
Bring all necessary equipment to patient's side; demonstrate professionalism and courtesy.
PPE - consider airborne or droplet precautions.
Initial assessment. BLS: consider Spinal Motion Restriction (SMR).
Pulse oximetry, supplemental oxygen, vital signs, temperature and blood glucose as indicated.
Consider cardiac monitor / 12-lead ECG.
Proceed to the appropriate protocol based on chief complaint.
If patient doesn't fit a protocol, contact OLMC (Online Medical Control).

pearls: For the purposes of this protocol, a pediatric patient is < 16 years old.
Any patient contact that does not result in transport requires documentation and disposition.
Required vital signs on every patient include BP, pulse, RR, pain/severity.
Pulse oximetry, glucose measurement, and temperature documentation is dependent on complaint.
Timing of transport based on patient's clinical condition.

steps.text: Scene safety; bring all necessary equipment to patient's side; demonstrate professionalism and courtesy.
PPE - consider airborne or droplet precautions.
Initial assessment. BLS: consider Spinal Motion Restriction.
Consider pulse oximetry, capnography, supplemental oxygen, pediatric vital signs, temperature and blood glucose as indicated.
Consider cardiac monitor / 12-lead ECG.
Proceed to the appropriate protocol based on chief complaint (e.g. Pediatric Cardiac Arrest -> Pediatric Pulseless Arrest).
If patient doesn't fit a protocol, contact OLMC.

differential: 5 H's: Hypovolemia, Hypoxia, Hydrogen ion (acidosis), Hypo/Hyperkalemia, Hypothermia/Hyperthermia
5 T's: Tension pneumothorax, Tamponade, Toxins (beta/calcium blockers, digoxin, antidepressants, cocaine), Thrombosis (PE), Thrombosis (coronary)
Other: Trauma, electrical shock, pacemaker failure
pearls: Always confirm asystole in more than one lead.
Always address correctable causes.

steps.text: Immediate uninterrupted CPR.
First airway: Supraglottic Airway (SGA) with EtCO2. If this fails, intubate through SGA or move to intubation with Video Laryngoscopy. Attach ResQPOD.
Adult IV/IO access.
Epinephrine 1 mg/10 mL - 1 mg IVP, IO. Repeat every 10 minutes. Maximum total 4 mg.
Identify / correct causes of asystole (H's and T's) - check Blood Glucose Analysis.
If available, POCUS (linear probe) may be used during pulse checks to assess for cardiac activity at the Common Carotid Artery (CCA). Limit time off chest < 10 seconds.
POCUS-assisted TOR guidelines: standard cardiac arrest care completed + asystole on monitor + absent CCA pulsation + persistently low EtCO2.
Persistent asystole after 30 minutes of high-quality CPR with BLS and ALS interventions -> move to Termination of Resuscitation (TOR) guideline.
AT ANY TIME ROSC achieved -> go to Post ROSC Care protocol.

differential: Overdose (TCAs, digoxin, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers)
pearls: Always address correctable causes.
Routine use of Sodium Bicarbonate, Dextrose, Naloxone and Calcium is NOT indicated unless a clinical scenario exists (e.g. blood sugar < 60; known IVDA; missed/on dialysis).

steps.text: Immediate uninterrupted CPR. Adult Airway & Adult IV/IO protocols.
Epinephrine 1 mg/10 mL - 1 mg IVP, IO. Repeat every 10 minutes. Maximum total 4 mg.
Consider H's and T's causes. Routine use of the following is NOT indicated unless clinical info suggests hypoglycemia, opiate overdose, or hyperkalemia:

Hypoglycemia suspected: Dextrose 10% (D10) - 5 gm IV Infusion (50 mL). Withdraw 50 mL from 250 mL NS bag, add 1 amp D50 = D10. Give 50 mL (5g) increments until normal mentation. Maximum total 25 gm (250 mL).
Opiate overdose suspected: Naloxone (Narcan) 2-4 mg IVP, IO.
Hyperkalemia arrest: Calcium Chloride 1 gm IVP, IO.
TCA / hyperkalemia / renal failure: Sodium Bicarbonate (1 mEq/mL) 1 mEq/kg IVP, IO.
Beta blocker overdose suspected: Glucagon 1 mg IVP.
Suspected tension pneumothorax: Needle Chest Decompression.

POCUS (if available): assess CCA during pulse checks, limit time off chest < 10 sec. Pseudo-PEA criteria: organized ECG + rising EtCO2 + visible CCA pulsation. If pseudo-PEA present: fluid resuscitate, begin Epinephrine infusion, treat reversible causes, pause CPR.
Criteria to discontinue: cease efforts per department guideline.
AT ANY TIME ROSC achieved -> go to Post ROSC Care protocol.

pearls: Reassess airway frequently.
Suspected HYPERKALEMIC arrest: give Calcium Chloride and Sodium Bicarbonate.
Torsades de Pointes: 2 grams Magnesium Sulfate.
Uninterrupted high-quality CPR and early defibrillation are key.
ALS crew discretion on advanced airway (SGA vs VL ETT).
Persistent VF/pulseless VT (>3 shocks): consider adjusting pad placement to Anterior/Posterior if not previously used.

steps.text: Defibrillation sequence: immediately defibrillate VF/Pulseless VT at 200, 300, 360 Joules. Immediately resume CPR.
Reassess rhythm and repeat every 2 minutes. Charge defibrillator at 1:45 in the 2-minute cycle. At 2 minutes: pulse check, med admin, defibrillate. Dump charge if rhythm becomes non-shockable.
CPR: immediate uninterrupted manual or automated CPR; use metronome and feedback device if available.
Adult Airway protocol; begin ventilation 10/min.
Epinephrine 1 mg/10 mL - 1 mg IVP, IO. Repeat every 10 minutes. Maximum total 4 mg.
Amiodarone (Cordarone) 300 mg IVP, IO. After 3-5 minutes, Amiodarone 150 mg IVP, IO.
Torsades de Pointes: Magnesium Sulfate 2 gm IVP.
Suspected hyperkalemia: Calcium Chloride 1 gm IVP, IO AND Sodium Bicarbonate 50 mEq IVP, IO.
Persistent VF/pulseless VT after 3 shocks: adjust pad placement to Anterior/Posterior if not previously used. Consider new pads following multiple defibrillations with original set.

Dual Sequential Defibrillation (DSD) - indications: refractory VF/pVT after 3 standard shocks. Procedure: bring 2nd defibrillator, apply 2nd set of patches (one set ant/post, other ant/lat), one paramedic operates both monitors, charge both to max joules, call 'CLEAR', push button on monitor #1 then immediately monitor #2 (not simultaneously), resume standard care. Subsequent VF/pVT: use DSD again at same (maximal) energy.
TOR (Termination of Resuscitation) criteria met? -> follow TOR guideline.
AT ANY TIME ROSC achieved -> go to Post ROSC Care protocol.

signs_symptoms: Location (substernal, epigastric, arm, jaw, neck, shoulder)
pearls: Avoid NTG in patients who used erectile dysfunction meds (Viagra, Levitra, Cialis) in the past 24 hours.
If patient has STEMI, establish a 2nd IV.
Monitor for hypotension after NTG administration.
Diabetic, geriatric, and female patients often have atypical symptoms.

steps.text: Oxygen to maintain SpO2 > 94%.
Aspirin 324 mg PO, unless allergy to ASA.
12-Lead ECG (EMT may set up and transmit).
Adult IV/IO protocol - prefer 2 saline locks. Avoid saline infusions in STEMI unless hypotensive (delays cath lab transit).
If Paramedic interprets 12-lead as STEMI: transmit 12-lead ECG, contact dispatch to pre-alert closest STEMI receiving facility, declare STEMI alert on transport.
Inferior MI? Do right-sided ECG (V4R). Use caution with nitroglycerin in Inferior MI (+V4R) WITHOUT adequate fluid resuscitation.
Hypotension? Normal Saline 0.9% 1 L Fluid Bolus and re-evaluate.
Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL (spray or tablet) every 5 minutes if SBP > 90.
Continued pain: Fentanyl (Sublimaze) 25-50 mcg IVP, up to 100 mcg.
May repeat Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL every 5 minutes if SBP > 90.
Hypotension / arrhythmia develops -> treat per that protocol.
Nausea/vomiting: consider Ondansetron (Zofran) 4 mg IVP, IM.

history: Blood loss: GI, AAA, ectopic, vaginal
differential: Shock: hypovolemic, cardiogenic, septic, neurogenic, anaphylactic
pearls: Hypotension = SBP < 90 mmHg.
Consider orthostatic vitals on non-trauma patients with suspected blood/fluid loss.
Vasopressors should be given through a large-bore antecubital site.
Use extreme caution with peripheral-line vasopressors; stop and notify receiving facility if any sign of infiltration.

steps.text: Treat per the appropriate trauma protocol instead of this one.
No rales present: Normal Saline 0.9% 500 mL Fluid Bolus.
Treat per the appropriate cardiac protocol.
Universal Patient Care, Adult IV/IO protocol.
Normal Saline 0.9% - 20 mL/kg Fluid Bolus.
SEPTIC SHOCK consideration: assure aggressive crystalloid given before vasopressors - Normal Saline 30 mL/kg Fluid Bolus. See Fever/Suspected Sepsis protocol.

Pressor needed (paramedic discretion)? Epinephrine Push Dose 10-20 mcg IVP, IO. Dilution: discard 9 mL of Epi 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL), draw up 9 mL NS to make Epi 1:100,000 (10 mcg/mL). Give 1-2 mL every 3 minutes until BP/HR goals achieved. LABEL syringe.
If pressor needed beyond push-dose: Epinephrine Drip 1 mg mixed into 1,000 mL NS (60 gtt set). Infuse until HR > 60 and MAP > 65 mmHg. LABEL the bag.
Observe and reassess.

history: Report of illicit drug use or ingestion
pearls: Safer to assume hypoglycemia than hyperglycemia if in doubt; recheck blood sugar after D10/glucagon.
Do not let alcohol confuse the clinical picture.
Do not give oral glucose if patient cannot protect airway.
Consider patient restraints.
Omit thiamine if no signs of malnutrition or alcoholism.

steps.text: Consider Spinal Motion Restriction (SMR).
Adult IV/IO protocol; Blood Glucose Analysis; 12-lead ECG.
If signs of shock: Normal Saline 0.9% 20 mL/kg Fluid Bolus.
Glucose abnormal? -> go to Hypoglycemia/Hyperglycemia protocol.
Hypotensive/shock? -> go to Hypotension/Shock Non-Trauma protocol.
Suspected overdose/toxic exposure? -> go to that protocol.
Fever/suspected sepsis? -> go to that protocol.
Arrhythmia present? -> go to specific protocol: Bradycardia-Unstable or Tachycardia w/Pulse (SVT, A-Fib/A-Flutter, VT).

pearls: Status Epilepticus: >2 successive seizures without a period of consciousness/recovery.
Grand mal: generalized - LOC, incontinence, tongue trauma.
Focal seizures (petit mal): only part of the body, no LOC.
Jacksonian seizures: focal seizures that become generalized.
Be prepared for airway problems and continued seizures.
Assess for occult trauma and substance abuse.
Be prepared to assist ventilation if midazolam is used.
Seizures in pregnant patients: follow Obstetrical Emergency.
Thiamine may be omitted if patient does not appear malnourished.

steps.text: Spinal Motion Restriction (SMR); check Blood Glucose Analysis.
No IV/IO access - Age < 65: Midazolam (Versed) 10 mg IM. Age > 65: Midazolam 5 mg IM.
IV/IO present: Midazolam (Versed) 2-5 mg IVP, IO.
Still seizing? Repeat Midazolam (Versed) 2-5 mg IVP, IO.
Recurrent/refractory seizure: Ketamine (Ketalar) (50 mg/mL) 1 mg/kg IVP, IO. Maximum dose 100 mg. Full monitoring mandatory including EtCO2. Consider intubation with Video Laryngoscopy.
Adult IV/IO protocol.
Blood Glucose Analysis.
Glucose < 60 mg/dL -> go to Hypoglycemia protocol.

pearls: Optimize scene/transport time if symptom onset < 24 hours.
Onset = last witnessed time patient was symptom-free.
Monitor for airway problems (swallowing, vomiting).
Always assess for hypoglycemia.
Document RACE score and 12-lead ECG.
Interventional stroke centers = transport to closest appropriate Comprehensive Stroke Center.

steps.text: Blood Glucose Analysis.
BEFAST exam / RACE Scoring Tool. If positive and symptoms < 24 hours: determine 'Last Known Well' time; bring patient ID to hospital for quick registration.
Adult IV/IO protocol; 12-Lead ECG.
Pediatric patient with suspected stroke? Transport to Pediatric Hospital (SVMMC or ProMedica Toledo Hospital ED).
Calculate RACE Scoring Tool. Score >= 5: declare 'RACE Alert', transport to closest Comprehensive Stroke or Thrombectomy-capable Center.
Score < 5: declare 'Stroke Alert', transport to closest Primary Stroke Center.
Primary Stroke Centers: Mercy St. Charles, Mercy St. Vincent, ProMedica Flower, ProMedica Bay Park, ProMedica Toledo Hospital, University of Toledo Medical Center.
Comprehensive Stroke Centers: Mercy St. Vincent, ProMedica Toledo Hospital. Thrombectomy-Capable: University of Toledo Medical Center.

pearls: ALWAYS give Epinephrine 1 mg/1 mL IM (never IV); 1 mg/10 mL may be given only as directed in the flowchart.
Monitor pulse ox continuously.
CPAP indicated in hypertensive pulmonary edema and COPD exacerbation with impending respiratory arrest.
Contact OLMC before epinephrine in patients > 50 years old, cardiac history, or HR > 150 - perform 12-lead ECG on these patients.
Record/monitor ETCO2 for respiratory distress patients.

steps.text: Follow Acute Pulmonary Edema protocol with immediate consideration of CPAP.
Contact OLMC if patient does not meet criteria for Epinephrine.
Adult IV/IO protocol. Consider CPAP for severe COPD.
Albuterol (Proventil) 2.5 mg NEB.
Albuterol 2.5 mg NEB mixed with Ipratropium (Atrovent) 0.5 mg NEB. May repeat x1.
Consider Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 125 mg IVP.
Consider Magnesium Sulfate 2 gm IV Infusion, mixed in 50 mL D5W, run wide open with 60 gtt set, delivered over 10-20 minutes.
Consider Epinephrine 1 mg/1 mL 0.5 mg IM. May repeat x1.
Adult IV/IO protocol. Nebulized Saline 3 mL.
If no improvement: Epinephrine 1 mg/1 mL 0.3-0.5 mg NEB mixed with 3 mL NS.
Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 125 mg IVP.
AEMT: Epinephrine 1 mg/1 mL 0.3-0.5 mg IM.
Adult Airway protocol as needed. For severe cases: Epinephrine 1 mg/10 mL (0.1 mcg/mL... i.e. 1:10,000) 1 mcg/kg IVP - each 1 mL = 100 mcg; typical adult dose ~100 mcg.
Position of comfort. CPAP settings range 5-10 cmH2O.
Anxiety/intolerance to CPAP, if SBP > 100 and not tolerating mask: Ketamine (Ketalar) (100 mg/mL) 0.5 mg/kg IN, IM, OR Ketamine 25 mg IVP, IO mixed with 50 mL NS over 10 minutes.
Additional sedation needed: Midazolam (Versed) 2-5 mg IVP, maximum 5 mg, OR Midazolam 2 mg IN if needed.

history: Ingestion or suspected ingestion of toxic substance
pearls: Do not rely on patient's history of ingestion in a suicide attempt.
Bring bottles to the ED.
Depressants: decreased HR/BP/temp/respirations, non-specific pupils.
Stimulants: increased HR/BP/temp, dilated pupils, seizures.
Anticholinergic: increased HR/temp, dilated pupils, mental status change.
Insecticides: increased/decreased HR, increased secretions, N/V/D, pinpoint pupils.
Consider restraints per policy.
ALS units may transport patients who received activated charcoal.

steps.text: EMT: Naloxone (Narcan) 2-4 mg IN.
AEMT/Paramedic: Naloxone (Narcan) 2-4 mg IN, IVP, IO, IM to reverse respiratory depression. May repeat x2.
Refusal of care? Follow Refusal Procedure.
Use co-oximetry (SpCO) to screen: headache, dizziness, weakness, confusion, LOC.
Treatment thresholds: COHb > 5% in non-smokers, > 10% in smokers.
Treatment: 100% Oxygen by NRB.
Hyperbaric facility consideration: COHb > 25-30%, neurological impairment, cardiac involvement, or pregnancy.
Beta blocker OD: Glucagon 1 mg IVP, IN, IM.
Calcium channel blocker OD: Calcium Chloride 1 gm Slow IVP.

Adult > 70 kg (154 lbs) with suspected cyanide poisoning: Cyanokit (Hydroxocobalamin) 5 gm IV Infusion. Add 200 mL NS to upright vial via transfer spike to fill line, invert 60 sec, use vented tubing + filter line, infuse over 15 minutes.
12-Lead ECG.
Sodium Bicarbonate (1 mEq/mL) 1-2 mEq/kg IVP for hypotension, seizures, ventricular dysrhythmias, or mental status changes.
Otherwise treat per the appropriate protocol for the presenting symptom.

pearls: Epinephrine may precipitate cardiac ischemia - use caution in patients > 50 years old; perform ECG.
Shorter onset = more severe reaction.

branches.label: Hives / Rash only - no respiratory component

steps.text: IV / cardiac monitor.
Diphenhydramine (Benadryl) 50 mg IVP, IM.
Reassess. If hypotension develops -> Hypotension protocol. If arrhythmia -> Arrhythmia protocol. If respiratory distress develops -> Respiratory Distress protocol.
IV / cardiac monitor.
EMT-Anaphylaxis only: Epinephrine 1 mg/1 mL 0.3 mg Auto-Injector, may repeat x1.
Epinephrine 1 mg/1 mL 0.5 mg IM. May repeat x1 in 5 minutes. If more than 2 IM doses needed, go to IV.
Paramedic only: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl) 50 mg IVP, IM.
Paramedic only: Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 125 mg IVP, IM.
Adult IV/IO, cardiac monitor.
Epinephrine 1 mg/1 mL 0.5 mg IM (Paramedic only). May repeat x1 in 5 minutes. If more than 2 IM doses needed, go to IV.
Epinephrine 1:10,000 (Epinephrine 1 mg/10 mL) 0.1 mg IVP (100 mcg). Give every minute until symptoms improve. NOTE: this is NOT the same as Push Dose Epinephrine.

No improvement, paramedic discretion, requires large-bore IV (18 or 16 gauge preferred): Epinephrine Push Dose 10-20 mcg IVP, IO. Dilution: discard 9 mL Epi 1:10,000, draw 9 mL NS to make 1:100,000 (10 mcg/mL). Give 1-2 mL every 3 minutes until BP/HR goals met. LABEL syringe.
Still refractory: Epinephrine Drip 1 mg mixed into 1,000 mL NS (60 gtt set). Infuse until HR > 60 and MAP > 65 mmHg. LABEL the bag.

branches.label: Crashing anaphylaxis (unconscious, requiring assisted ventilations, apneic, or arrested)

steps.text: Give Epinephrine as above.
Intubate - first best attempt, no SGA, needs ETT.

history: Report of illicit drug use or ingestion
pearls: Be aware of AMS as a sign of environmental toxin or Haz-Mat exposure.
Safer to assume hypoglycemia than hyperglycemia if in doubt.
Low glucose < 60, normal 60-120, high > 250.

steps.text: Consider Spinal Motion Restriction.
Pediatric Universal Care, Pediatric IV/IO, Blood Glucose.
If signs of shock: Normal Saline 0.9% 20 mL/kg Fluid Bolus.
Glucose abnormal? -> go to Pediatric Hypoglycemia/Hyperglycemia protocol.
Shock present? -> go to Pediatric Hypotension/Sepsis/Shock Non-Trauma protocol.
Suspected overdose/toxic/cyanide exposure? -> go to that protocol.
Fever/suspected sepsis? -> go to that protocol.
Arrhythmia? -> go to specific protocol: Pediatric Bradycardia or Pediatric Tachycardia w/Pulse.

signs_symptoms: Hot, dry skin or elevated body temperature
pearls: Status Epilepticus: >2 successive seizures without a period of consciousness/recovery.
Be prepared to assist ventilation if Versed is used.
Immobilize the spine if trauma suspected.
In an infant, a seizure may be the only evidence of a closed head injury.

steps.text: Pediatric Airway protocol as needed.
Pediatric IV/IO; Blood Glucose.
Glucose < 60 mg/dL -> go to Pediatric Hypoglycemia/Hyperglycemia protocol.
Midazolam (Versed) (5 mg/mL) 0.2 mg/kg IN, IM, IVP, IO. May repeat x1. Maximum dosing 5 mg.
Continued seizure activity after 2 doses of midazolam: Ketamine (Ketalar) (50 mg/mL) 1 mg/kg IVP, IO. Maximum 100 mg. Be prepared to assist ventilations / place SGA.
Fever present? Begin cooling measures.

pearls: Pulse oximetry should be monitored continuously.
Do not force a child into a position - allow position of comfort.
Bronchiolitis (viral, typically infants) may not respond to albuterol.
Croup (<2 yrs, viral) - fever, gradual onset, no drooling.
Epiglottitis (>2 yrs, bacterial) - fever, rapid onset, possible stridor, common drooling.

steps.text: Albuterol (Proventil) 2.5 mg NEB. May repeat x1. Monitor and transport.
For severe cases, consider Epinephrine 1 mg/mL 0.01 mg/kg IM. Maximum 0.5 mg (0.5 mL).

branches.label: Wheezes, age > 1 year or history of wheeze

steps.text: Assessment: alertness, skin color/tone, work of breathing, accessory muscle use, nasal flaring, grunting, fever, cough.
Supplemental oxygen/respiratory support via nasal cannula, NRB, or CPAP with RAM cannula.
Albuterol (Proventil) 2.5 mg NEB mixed with Ipratropium (Atrovent) 0.5 mg NEB. May repeat x1.
Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) (62.5 mg/mL) 2 mg/kg IVP, IM. Maximum 125 mg (2 mL).
For severe cases, consider Epinephrine 1 mg/mL 0.01 mg/kg IM. Maximum 0.5 mg (0.5 mL).
No improvement, consider Pediatric IV if SpO2 < 92%.
Nebulized Saline 3 mL.
Epinephrine 1 mg/1 mL 0.5 mg NEB (0.5 mL mixed in 3 mL NS, nebulized).

pearls: Any patient with respiratory symptoms or extensive reaction should receive epinephrine and IV/IM Benadryl.
Shorter onset = more severe reaction.

steps.text: Pediatric IV; cardiac monitor.
Diphenhydramine (Benadryl) (50 mg/mL) 1 mg/kg IVP, IM. Maximum 25 mg (0.5 mL).
Reassess.
Pediatric IV; cardiac monitor.
Epinephrine 1 mg/mL 0.01 mg/kg IM. Maximum 0.5 mg (0.5 mL). EMT permitted to administer if patient in anaphylaxis.
Diphenhydramine (Benadryl) (50 mg/mL) 1 mg/kg IVP, IM. Maximum 25 mg (0.5 mL).
Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) (62.5 mg/mL) 2 mg/kg IVP, IM. Maximum 125 mg (2 mL).
Epi-Pen: may assist patient with their own Epi-Pen.

Epinephrine Push Dose 10-20 mcg IVP, IO. Dilution: discard 9 mL Epi 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL), draw 9 mL NS to make Epi 1:100,000 (10 mcg/mL). Give 1-2 mL every 3 minutes until BP/HR goals met. LABEL syringe.

history: Medications (beta-blocker, calcium channel blocker, clonidine, digoxin)
pearls: Use of lidocaine in heart block can worsen bradycardia and lead to asystole or death.
Pharmacologic treatment is based on presence/absence of symptoms - if symptomatic, treat; if asymptomatic, monitor only.
Consider treatable causes (e.g. beta or calcium channel blocker OD).
Remember to oxygenate and support ventilatory effort.

steps.text: 12-Lead ECG (EMT may set up and transmit). Adult IV/IO protocol. Fluid bolus as needed.
Atropine 1 mg IVP, IO. May repeat every 3-5 minutes. Maximum total 3 mg.
Consider immediate Transcutaneous Pacing in unstable patients with high-degree heart block when IV access not available.

No improvement, poor peripheral perfusion, altered mental status, hypotension - consider sedation with: Ketamine (Ketalar) (50 mg/mL) 0.2 mg/kg IVP, IO, maximum single dose 25 mg, may repeat x1 in 10 min to total max 50 mg.
OR Ketamine (Ketalar) (100 mg/mL) 0.5 mg/kg IN, IM. May repeat x1 in 10 minutes. Maximum single dose 25 mg, total max 50 mg.
Additional sedation required: Midazolam (Versed) 2 mg IVP, IO, IN. Maximum dose 4 mg.
Refractory: Epinephrine Drip 1 mg mixed into 1,000 mL NS (60 gtt set). Infuse until HR > 60 and MAP > 65 mmHg. LABEL the bag.

history: Related diseases: diabetes, CVA, renal failure, cardiac
pearls: Never treat elevated blood pressure based on one set of vital signs.
Symptomatic hypertension usually reveals through end-organ damage to cardiac, CNS, or renal systems.
Transport symptomatic hypertensive patients with head elevated.
Adverse reactions to treatment: thrombophlebitis, headache, flushing, tachycardia, dizziness, nausea.

steps.text: Check BP in both arms manually. 12-Lead ECG (EMT may set up and transmit). Adult IV/IO protocol.
Acute stroke suspected: DO NOT lower blood pressure.
Acute MI, not Inferior STEMI: administer SL Nitroglycerin per Chest Pain protocol.
Note: routine lowering of blood pressure in the field is NOT indicated except in the above scenarios.

differential: Continue to address specific differential with original arrhythmia.
pearls: Avoid hyperventilation.
Most patients post-resuscitation will require ventilatory assistance.
Post-resuscitation condition of patient changes rapidly.
Consult OLMC as needed regarding management.

steps.text: Goals of care: MAP > 65 mmHg. Oxygenation target SpO2 94-98%. Ventilation target EtCO2 35-45 mmHg. Temperature control - avoid shivering/fever.

Post-ROSC 10-minute monitoring goals: perform 12-Lead ECG, anticipate hypotension (prepare epi drip), plan for packaging/egress, monitor EtCO2/BP/pulse ox/ECG, attend to goals of care, anticipate sedation needs.
Adult IV/IO protocol. Monitor EtCO2 (>20 mmHg) with RR 10/min. DO NOT HYPERVENTILATE.
Dysrhythmia present? Go to the appropriate protocol (e.g. Bradycardia).
Hypotension (non-cardiac, non-trauma)? Consider Normal Saline 0.9% 20 mL/kg Fluid Bolus to achieve MAP > 65 mmHg.
Refractory: Epinephrine Drip 1 mg mixed into 1,000 mL NS (60 gtt set). Infuse until HR > 60 and MAP > 65 mmHg. LABEL the bag.
Post-ROSC sedation, 1st line: Fentanyl (Sublimaze) 50-100 mcg IVP, IO WITH Midazolam (Versed) 2.5-5 mg IVP, IO. May repeat x1.
Additional sedation required: Ketamine (Ketalar) 50-100 mg IVP, IO. May repeat 50-100 mg x1. Maximum 200 mg.
Paralysis required to avoid extubation? Vecuronium (Norcuron) 10 mg IVP, IO. Not for patients with a supraglottic airway.

history: Medications (theophylline, diet pills, thyroid, decongestants, digoxin)
signs_symptoms: Possible rhythms: sinus tach, atrial fib/flutter, multifocal atrial tachycardia
pearls: Do not give AV nodal blockers (diltiazem, beta blockers, digoxin) to suspected pre-excited atrial fib/flutter (WPW).
Paramedic may maintain diltiazem infusions begun at referring facilities - discontinue if hypotension, bradycardia, or allergic reaction occurs; notify OLMC.
Document all effects of therapy/rhythm changes.
Maximum dose Diltiazem is 10 mg per dose.

steps.text: Airway, breathing, circulation. Oxygen as indicated. Apply monitor / fast patches, pulse ox, BP. 12-lead ECG.
Identify and treat underlying cause.
Tachycardia causing hypotension, AMS, shock, ischemic chest pain, or acute heart failure? If unstable, go to Synchronized Cardioversion.
Synchronized Cardioversion: 100J, may escalate to 200J, 300J, 360J.
Sedation for cardioversion: Ketamine (Ketalar) (50 mg/mL) 0.2 mg/kg IVP, IO. May repeat x1. Maximum 25 mg.
OR Ketamine (Ketalar) (100 mg/mL) 0.5 mg/kg IN.
Additional sedation needed: Midazolam (Versed) 2.5 mg IVP, IO, IN, IM. May repeat x1.
Vagal maneuvers first.
1st dose: Adenosine (Adenocard) 6 mg Rapid IVP. Always flush with NS after each dose.
2nd dose: Adenosine (Adenocard) 12 mg Rapid IVP.
3rd dose: Adenosine (Adenocard) 12 mg Rapid IVP.
Check for WPW (short PR, delta wave, wide complex, RVR) - if suspected WPW, do NOT use Diltiazem.
Diltiazem (Cardizem) 10 mg Slow IVP. May repeat x1. Do not use in suspected WPW.

branches.label: Wide complex (>0.12 sec), regular — VT with pulse

steps.text: Amiodarone (Cordarone) 150 mg IV Infusion over 10 minutes. Mix 150 mg in 250 mL D5W, infuse over 10 min with 10 gtt set at 4 drops/sec = 250 drops/min.

history: Source of infection: illness, recent surgery/procedure, respiratory/GI/GU, recent antibiotics/steroids/immunosuppressants
signs_symptoms: Vital sign warnings: Temp > 38 or < 36; Pulse > 90 bpm; BP < 90 systolic or MAP < 65; RR > 20; EtCO2 < 26
pearls: SIRS = fever >38 or <36, HR >90, RR >20, arterial PCO2 <32.
Sepsis = one or more end organs begin to fail. Septic shock = sustained hypotension after aggressive fluid resuscitation.
Avoid hypoxia - adequately oxygenate; consider CPAP for moderate respiratory distress, intubate for AMS/respiratory failure.
Avoid overventilation to prevent acute lung injury.
Avoid pressor therapy until adequate fluid resuscitation performed.

steps.text: Consider droplet, airborne, contact precautions.
Assess pulse, RR, BP, EtCO2, temperature. Support airway. Establish 2 large-bore IVs.
Normal Saline 0.9% 30 mL/kg Fluid Bolus.
Reassess vitals/lung sounds. Notify receiving facility of suspected sepsis.

history: Exposure to environment, even in normal temperatures.
differential: CNS dysfunction: CVA; head injury; spinal cord injury.

Extremes of age susceptible.

Shivering stops below 32 C (90 F).

Remove wet clothing.
Handle very gently.
Blankets / external rewarming.

signs_symptoms: Heat Exhaustion: altered mental status, dizziness, nausea & vomiting, headache, elevated core body temperature.

Older or ill incapacitated patient, a failing of the temperature regulating center.

Consider cold packs to major artery sites.

Monitor and reassess.
Appropriate protocol based on patient symptoms.

Patient with duly executed DNR who is apneic.
Patient for whom resuscitation efforts are ceased on-scene.

differential: Attended death: death is attended when a person passes away in the presence of family and friends.

Attended death also includes: patient in a hospital or medical center; a resident of long-term care or nursing facility; an individual in hospice care; an individual in regular contact with a primary care physician who has suffered from an extended illness; the individual saw a primary care physician within a 30-day period prior to death.
Unattended death: a death in which the body is not found for days, weeks, or in some cases, months.

steps.text: Patient meets criteria for obvious death? In the opinion of the paramedic on scene, resuscitation would be futile or would fail to produce a positive outcome.
Contact law enforcement and/or county coroner.
Leave all medical devices in place. If devices have been removed, tape them to the chest of the patient.
Do not place sharps under tape; note them on the tape.
Monitor vital signs.
Adult IV/IO Protocol.
Administer Diphenhydramine (Benadryl) 50 mg IVP, IO, IM.
No improvement? Midazolam (Versed) 2.5 mg IVP, IO, IM.
Transport to closest appropriate ED.

Ice pack.

Adult IV/IO Protocol.
Normal Saline 0.9% (NS) 500 mL fluid bolus.
Reassess.

For patients with advanced airway needing sedation: Midazolam (Versed) (5 mg/mL) 0.1 mg/kg IVP. Maximum 5 mg.
Additional sedation needed? Ketamine (Ketalar) 25 mg IV Infusion. Mix 25 mg in 50 mL D5W and infuse over 10 minutes.
OR Ketamine (Ketalar) (100 mg/mL) 1 mg/kg IN. Divided between nares. Maximum 1 mL/nostril.

pearls: Exam: mental status; extremities; neuro.
In amputations, time is critical. Consider transport to pediatric trauma center.
Hip dislocation and knee and elbow fracture/dislocations have a high incidence of vascular compromise.
Urgently transport any injury with vascular compromise.
Blood loss may be concealed or not apparent with extremity injuries.
Severe bleeding not rapidly controlled may necessitate application of a tourniquet.
Lacerations must be evaluated for repair within 6 hours from the time of injury.

steps.text: If not an isolated extremity injury, go to Pediatric Multiple Trauma Protocol.
Immobilize extremity as indicated. Apply ice to reduce swelling.
Wound care/hemorrhage control.
Limb or life threatening event? Control life threatening hemorrhage with CAT Tourniquet. See: Wound Care/CAT Tourniquet.
Pain medication needed? Pediatric IV Protocol. Pediatric Pain Control Protocol.
Amputation? Clean amputated part. Wrap part in sterile dressing soaked with normal saline. Place in air tight container. Place container on ice if available.

Suspected Open Fractures: Do not reduce suspected open fractures such as a femur fracture with a traction splint unless there are no detectable distal pulses. If distal pulses are absent, apply gentle inline traction until pulses return.
